# Dell PowerSwitch — SmartFabric OS10 (OS10 Enterprise Edition) — Overview

Full-tier vendor doc (per [ROADMAP.md](../../ROADMAP.md) Phase 0 decision, 2026-07-16) — Dell's PowerSwitch/OS10 line is a genuine enterprise/datacenter NOS in active production use, not a lighter SMB product, so it gets the same depth as Cisco/Arista/Juniper/Huawei/Extreme/Aruba rather than the appendix-tier single-file treatment.

## Scope: OS10 only — Dell's switch line has three unrelated operating systems, not one

This is the same kind of dialect-fragmentation warning given in [`vendors/aruba/overview.md`](../aruba/overview.md) for HPE/Aruba, and it matters just as much here — do not assume "Dell switch" implies one CLI:

- **SmartFabric OS10 / OS10 Enterprise Edition** (this doc's scope) — the modern, Linux-based (Debian kernel, ONIE-installable) NOS for PowerSwitch **S-series and Z-series** models with **"-ON"** in the name (e.g. S5248F-ON, S5296F-ON, Z9332F-ON). This is Dell's current datacenter/spine-leaf target and what SignalScope should target for Dell support.
- **OS9 / FTOS (Force10 heritage)** — the CLI predecessor to OS10, still shipping on some legacy S-series hardware. Dell acquired Force10 Networks, and OS9 is that codebase's continuation; OS9's CLI is broadly IOS-like (closer in spirit to Cisco than OS10's own dialect, per Dell's own "OS9-to-OS10 Command Mapping" tech sheet, which exists precisely because the two are different enough to need one). Not covered further here.
- **DNOS 6.x (N-Series)** — an entirely separate operating system for Dell's **N-Series campus switches**, described by Dell as "the latest version of the PowerConnect operating system, running on a Linux kernel." **OS10 is explicitly not an upgrade path for N-Series** — Dell's own documentation states this directly. Not covered further here, and should not be assumed to share any CLI syntax with OS10 despite both running on Linux.

If SignalScope needs N-Series or OS9/legacy-S-series support later, each warrants its own research pass rather than being folded into this folder, exactly as `vendors/aruba/overview.md` recommends for its own legacy dialects.

## CLI dialect

OS10's CLI is a traditional line-mode shell (`configure terminal` → mode contexts) **deliberately IOS-like at the surface** — `interface`, `shutdown`/`no shutdown`, `switchport mode trunk`, `channel-group <n> mode active`, `spanning-tree` — while running on top of a genuinely different substrate (Debian Linux, with the CLI itself documented as "an OS10-specific command shell that runs on top of a Linux-based OS kernel," and a `system bash`-style Linux shell separately accessible per Dell's "Linux shell commands" documentation page). Interface names use a `ethernet <node>/<slot>/<port>` three-part scheme (e.g. `ethernet 1/1/2`), closer to Huawei's/Aruba's three-part convention than Cisco's two-part `GigabitEthernet0/1`.

## Config-apply model: immediate-apply by default, with an opt-in candidate/commit mode

This is OS10's most architecturally interesting feature relative to every other vendor in this docs tree, and worth getting right rather than assuming either the Cisco pattern or the Junos pattern applies uniformly:

- **Default behavior is immediate-apply**, identical in shape to Cisco/Arista/Huawei/Aruba: `configure terminal` → `interface ethernet 1/1/2` → `no shutdown` takes effect on the running configuration as each line is entered, no commit required. `write memory` persists to the startup configuration, the same Cisco/Arista-shorthand save semantics documented in [`comparison/cli-syntax-matrix.md`](../../comparison/cli-syntax-matrix.md).
- **A separate, opt-in "candidate configuration" / transaction-based mode exists**, entered explicitly with `start transaction` **before** `configure terminal` (not a flag on `configure terminal` itself, confirmed from Dell's own "How to use Transaction-Based Configuration Mode" KB article). Once in this mode, ordinary config commands are staged into a candidate buffer rather than applied immediately — `show candidate-configuration` reviews staged changes, `show diff candidate-configuration running-configuration` diffs staged-vs-live, `commit` applies the whole staged set, `discard` abandons it.
- **SignalScope implication**: this is architecturally closest to Junos's candidate/commit model (see [`comparison/cli-syntax-matrix.md`](../../comparison/cli-syntax-matrix.md)) but strictly **opt-in per session** rather than the vendor default — the reverse of Aruba's `checkpoint auto <n>` (which layers a rollback *safety net* on top of an always-immediate-apply base) and structurally different again from Junos (where candidate/commit is the *only* way to change config at all). SignalScope's session-state tracker needs a third state for OS10 specifically: "immediate-apply session" (default) vs. "transaction-mode session" (after `start transaction`), with the GUI's Save/Apply affordance behaving like Cisco's in the first case and like Junos's in the second — and the terminal must show the `start transaction` line itself when SignalScope chooses to use this mode, per the "no hidden setup commands" principle in [`connectivity-methods.md`](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md).

## SNMP version support

v1, v2c, and v3 are all supported (`snmp-server` command family: `snmp-server user`, `snmp-server host`, `snmp-server engineID`, `snmp-server view`, `snmp-server community` — confirmed from Dell's own SmartFabric OS10 User Guide command pages). SNMPv3 supports the standard USM auth (MD5/SHA)/privacy (DES/AES) split, remote-engine users (`snmp-server engineID` must be configured before a remote user), and MIB-view-based access restriction (`snmp-server view <name> <oid-tree> {included|excluded}`) — structurally similar to Huawei VRP's `snmp-agent mib-view` access-control model documented in [`vendors/huawei/mib-reference.md`](../huawei/mib-reference.md); the view/group/community wiring is now first-hand-confirmed (Phase 2, 2026-07-22) from the full User Guide PDF's SNMP chapter — `read-write`/`read-only`/`notify` views exist and are assignable per-group, but this is the SNMP **agent's own access-control layer**, not evidence that any particular managed object accepts a SET (see write-scope finding below).

**Practical write scope — re-researched Phase 2 (2026-07-22), first-hand primary source**: obtained and read the complete SNMP/MIBs chapter of Dell's own SmartFabric OS10 User Guide (Release 10.5.0, full PDF, not a search-summary or JS-truncated portal fetch — see updated sources list below). Two firm findings:
1. **OS10's own MIB list is complete and thin**: 22 standard MIBs (Table 5) and exactly **five** Dell EMC enterprise MIBs (Table 6): `DELLEMC-OS10-BGP4V2-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-CHASSIS-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-PRODUCTS-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-SMI-MIB`, `DELLEMC-OS10-TC-MIB`. None of these five is a configuration-action MIB analogous to Cisco's `CISCO-VLAN-MEMBERSHIP-MIB`/`CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` or Aruba's `ARUBAWIRED-PORTSECURITY-MIB`/`ARUBAWIRED-CONFIG-MIB`/`ARUBAWIRED-MSTP-MIB` — BGP4V2 and CHASSIS are monitoring/inventory-shaped, PRODUCTS is a `sysObjectID`-style identity tree (see `mib-reference.md`), SMI/TC are base type-definition modules with no managed objects of their own. **Unlike every other full-tier vendor in this project, OS10 ships no enterprise MIB at all that targets VLAN membership, port-security, STP-hardening, or config-save/checkpoint as an SNMP action.**
2. The guide's own summary line is: *"OS10 supports standard and private SNMP MIBs, including all get requests."* This phrasing is suggestive (it markedly does not say "and set requests") but not a conclusive "GET-only" statement on its own — flagged as a signal, not treated as proof.

This corrects a prior-session claim: an earlier pass (search-summary-sourced) asserted Dell's OS10 User Guide states "partial implementations of RFC 4188 (BRIDGE-MIB) and RFC 4363 (Q-BRIDGE-MIB) are supported." **That sentence does not appear anywhere in the actual MIBs chapter** (verified by a full-text read of the PDF, `grep -i partial` across the entire ~80,000-line converted text returns nothing relevant to MIB support) — Table 5 lists `BRIDGE-MIB`/`Q-BRIDGE-MIB` plainly, with no partial/full qualifier. Treat the "partial implementation" claim as retracted; it was likely a search-engine-summary artifact rather than actual page content.

**Net conclusion**: because no Dell enterprise MIB provides a documented config-write workflow, the only theoretical SNMP-write path for VLAN/PVID assignment on OS10 would be the standard `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` object itself (declared read-write in the base IETF MIB, same as for every other vendor in this project) — but no OS10-specific documentation confirms the agent actually honors a SET on it, and none was found for `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` either. This is now a **verified-absence-of-documentation** finding (first-hand read of the complete MIB list) rather than a research gap — a meaningfully stronger negative than the prior "not investigated" status, even though the practical guidance is unchanged: **treat all OS10 configuration as CLI-only** per [`gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md).

## MIB licensing / redistribution note

Dell hosts a MIB-file download (`Current_MIBs_pkb_en_US_1.tar`/`.zip`) as an attachment on its own support KB article for **OS9** MIBs specifically (covering releases 9.8.0.0 through 9.14.2.1, originally hosted on force10networks.com before Dell's acquisition folded it into the Dell support portal). **No explicit license or redistribution terms are stated on that page** — the same situation as Huawei and Extreme (see [`vendors/huawei/mibs/README.md`](../huawei/mibs/README.md) and [`vendors/extreme/mibs/README.md`](../extreme/mibs/README.md) for the identical reasoning applied there). OS10's own MIBs are shipped **on-device** (per Dell's SmartFabric OS10 User Guide, at `/opt/dell/os10/snmp/mibs/`) rather than offered as a separate portal download in what this session's research surfaced. **No Dell/Force10 MIB files are vendored in this repo's `mibs/` folder** — see [`mibs/README.md`](mibs/README.md) for source links instead.

**Uncertainty flags for implementers**: unlike the Tier-1 vendors researched in the original documentation pass (Cisco/Arista/Extreme/Huawei/Juniper/Aruba/MikroTik), this vendor's research this session was conducted via search-summary results and targeted page fetches rather than full primary-document reads throughout — several claims below (SNMPv3 view/group wiring, exact paging-disable command, port-security violation-action keyword set) should be treated as **directionally correct but not verified to the same first-hand-read standard** as the original seven vendors, and re-confirmed against the full SmartFabric OS10 User Guide PDF before production use.
